sources.title: BIPM: SI base units
sources.supports: Mass is an SI base quantity with kilogram (kg) as its unit; this does not determine the mass of any pictured object.

sources.title: NIST: SI Units - Mass
sources.supports: Distinguishes inertial mass from gravitational/support force; everyday weighing language can denote mass, whereas scientific weight is a force expressed in newtons. Only its current SI/FAQ sections are used, not the obsolete prototype-as-primary-standard paragraph.

sources.title: JCGM VIM3 1.19: quantity value
sources.supports: A quantity value retains both its number and reference; mass examples use a stated body and a unit.

sources.title: JCGM VIM3 2.9: measurement result
sources.supports: A measurement result attributes quantity values to a measurand with relevant information; uncertainty normally accompanies a measured value. This motivates keeping a source declaration separate from a measurement claim.

sources.title: JCGM VIM3 4.1: indication
sources.supports: An instrument indication can take visual numeric or pointer form; indication and measured quantity need not even be the same kind. A visible display alone is insufficient to certify the depicted object mass.

sources.title: JCGM VIM3 2.3: measurand
sources.supports: The quantity intended for measurement must retain its kind, carrying body or substance, relevant components and state. This supports preserving independently declared owner scope and conditions, not inferring them from an image.

sources.title: JCGM VIM3 1.1: quantity
sources.supports: A quantity is a property carried by a phenomenon, body or substance, with magnitude expressed using a number and reference. The generalized mass-preservation option keeps that carrier relationship.

baseline_top8.meaning: Show a complete instant print as a physical card with an image window, border, thickness, and supported contact.

A photographic visual relation owned by physical photographic object and output container in which transparent film frame, cardboard or plastic mount, transmitted-light viewing, image contained within mount aperture, and film edge density or thickness coexist as evidence in one physical image.

A physical photographic print containing a clearly adult subject is itself captured or scanned as a material object. Complete print edges, substrate thickness or curl, surrounding album or scanner context, and localized physical wear coexist. The material lineage is visible, while age, provenance, rarity, and who owned the print remain metadata claims.

confusion_boundaries: Mass in grams/kilograms is not gravitational force in newtons. Everyday source wording weighs in kg can retain its stated mass meaning without unit conversion.
A number plus unit belongs to one declared object/part and stated assembled/net/condition basis; it cannot migrate to an adjacent component or whole assembly.

Qualitative physically heavy/lightweight is valid if explicit; it need not be deleted for lack of a numeral. Heavy-looking, dense-looking, dark, large, thick, compressed, metallic or airy alone cannot supply actual mass.
A visible scale, pointer or number is an indication or scene text, not independent verification of object mass. No text, display, caption or weighing event is added by a mass-only record.
Apparent effort, flexed arms, compression, support, torque and buoyancy do not determine mass or physical ability.
Coronal mass ejection, hair mass, social mass, visual balance and metaphorical weight are separate meanings.
The role does not create people, infer body weight, change human anatomy or override adult/domain conditions.

Preserving a declared mass is a PR obligation when explicitly requested; a selected same-value mass effect still retains its actual material/property locks. All actual effects and owner scopes require native review.
